analysis.title: Walmart Inc. (WMT): First Take: 3Q earnings beat; FY26 guidance raised
key_insights: WMT reported 3Q26 adj. EPS of $0.65 versus GS and FactSet consensus of $0.64. Total revenue was $188,835mn versus a GS estimate of $187,619mn and consensus of $187,379mn.
Walmart US same-store sales rose 2.9%, in line with consensus. Traffic added 1.5% and average ticket 1.4%. Pharmacy deflation was a net headwind of about 70 bps.
Grocery sales grew mid-single digits, led by pantry, with like-for-like inflation of 1.4%. General merchandise grew low-single digits, led by toys and auto care, with like-for-like inflation of 0.3%.
Health and wellness sales fell low-single digits. Pharmacy script counts grew mid-single digits with market share gains, offset by an impact of about 800 bps from Maximum Fair Pricing legislation.

Global eCommerce net sales grew 17% (2Q: 23%) and Walmart US eCommerce grew 23% (2Q: 24%). Global advertising grew 25% including VIZIO and Walmart US advertising grew 36% ex VIZIO and Vibe, down from 38% and 43% in 2Q.

WMT raised FY guidance at the midpoint: net sales growth of 4.9-5.2% (prior 4.0-5.0%), adj. operating income growth of 8.0-8.6% (prior 7.0-8.5%) and adj. EPS of $2.84-2.89 (prior $2.80-2.87). The sales guide is below GS/consensus of 5.5%/5.6%, and the EPS guide is below GS at $2.90 and in line with consensus at $2.89 at the top end.
Gross margin was 24.5%, up 28 bps y/y and above the consensus-aligned estimate of 24.2%. Walmart US gross margin rose 50 bps on digital advertising mix and lower-priced pharmacy mix from deflation.

SG&A grew 6.8% y/y and the expense ratio was 21.5%, up 34 bps y/y and above the 21.2% estimate. Walmart US expense ratio rose 45 bps on depreciation from capital investment and higher self-insured general liability claims.
EBIT was $7,770mn versus GS $7,577mn and consensus $7,576mn. EBIT margin was 4.1% versus the 4.0% estimate.
Total inventory grew 8.1% against total sales growth of 5.1%. Walmart US inventory grew 5.2% y/y on strategic initiatives and cost inflation.

The stock was down about 1% pre-market. GS will ask on the call about quarter-to-date trends, inflation, grocery and general merchandise promotions, operating income dollar growth, tariff refunds and updated guidance.

market_movers.rationale: Buy rating and $132 12-month target are based on a risk-reward framework with downside/base/upside relative P/E multiples of 160%/165%/170%. The stock closed at $127.36 on 18 Nov 2026, implying 3.6% upside.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 adj. EPS reported $0.65 vs GS and FactSet consensus estimates of $0.64, and $0.62 in 3Q25 (+4.5% y/y). Reported 11/19/2026.
3Q26 total revenue reported $188,835mn (+5.2% y/y) vs GS estimate $187,619mn and consensus $187,379mn.
3Q26 reported operating profit $7,770mn (+7.0% y/y) vs GS estimate $7,577mn and consensus $7,576mn. Operating margin 4.1% vs 4.0% estimate.
3Q26 reported net income $5,184mn (+3.8% y/y) vs GS estimate $5,124mn. Tax rate was 24.5% vs a 24.0% estimate.

FY guidance (company, issued 11/19/2026): net sales growth 4.9-5.2%, adj. operating income growth 8.0-8.6%, adj. EPS $2.84-2.89. GS estimates FY EPS of $2.90 (consensus $2.89) and net sales growth of 5.5% (consensus 5.6%).
GS quarterly EPS estimates: 4Q (10/26E column) $0.64, then $0.79 and $0.72 for the following two quarters. The table lists 7/26 actual EPS of $0.81.
risk_factors: Inability to use expense leverage to offset investments in e-commerce and pricing.
Pressure from wages or transportation costs.
